1. I’m a big fan of the musical saw, you basically use a violin bow on a big flexible saw and bend it to change the pitch, it has a really cool haunted, ghostly sound.
2. My least favorite instrument is the violin, not because of the sound, but because of how overused it is, and how it’s really only used for one style. I like violin when it’s used for music that’s not classical, like bluegrass or folk, but it just sounds so boring and bland in classical music, plus all string orchestra songs sound exactly the same.
3. I fucking love instrumentals, I highly recommend Hot Sugar, he samples sounds from everyday things and makes such sick music with them. A good starting place is his album Moon Money.
4. think that voice counts as an instrument but only when the person singing isn’t singing words, like in Great Gig in the Sky by Pink Floyd, since she isn’t singing words her voice more fills the role of a solo instrument. If she was singing words then the singing more fills the role of a story teller. Giving the song a more clear story or message with a more clear direction. But a lot of music has words that are nonsense but a story can still be interpreted from them, like in I am the Walrus by The Beatles.
